title: JANUS Engine R0A4F — low-adhesion Axle-cylinder wall and dual-zone anti-scale surface
purpose: Make the inner cylindrical wall thermodynamically and mechanically unfavorable for persistent CaCO3 attachment while remaining compatible with Axle wiping, water chemistry, POMS, seals and long-duration operation.
design_principle: Do not optimize contact angle alone. Optimize measured CaCO3 adhesion, wall deposit mass, coating wear, corrosion, Axle torque and O2-system compatibility under the actual JANUS water chemistry.

ZONE_A_WIPED_TRACK.role: surface repeatedly approached or contacted by sacrificial/compliant Axle scraper edges
preferred_surface_character: chemically stable in low-mineral recirculating water
repairable or replaceable liner where practical
ZONE_A_WIPED_TRACK.candidate_family: fluorinated diamond-like-carbon or other hard low-adhesion coating on polished stainless substrate
ZONE_A_WIPED_TRACK.reason: DLC-class surfaces combine hardness and corrosion/wear resistance; fluorinated DLC has literature precedent for reduced mineral-scale adhesion. Micro/nanotextured superhydrophobic surfaces may be damaged by repeated wiping and therefore are not the default contact track.

preferred_surface_character: stable under continuous shear and immersion
ZONE_B_NONCONTACT_WALL.candidate_family: silicone-nanofilament or other durable superhydrophobic anti-scale coating
ZONE_B_NONCONTACT_WALL.literature_screen: A 2025 steel-coating study reported 75.5% lower CaCO3 deposition for a silicone-nanofilament superhydrophobic coating than its uncoated steel control under that study's conditions.
ZONE_B_NONCONTACT_WALL.boundary: This percentage is not transferable to JANUS without testing. Mechanical durability, wetting-state collapse, chemistry drift and membrane compatibility remain open gates.

baseline_controls: uncoated reference coupon of the final chamber alloy

literature_anchors.finding: calcite attachment depends on substrate surface energy, van der Waals attraction and electrostatic double-layer interactions; stainless steel in that comparison had lower surface energy than several tested metals
bioinspired silicone-nanofilament superhydrophobic coating on steel reduced CaCO3 deposition by 75.5% in the reported test and showed high-shear resilience

literature_anchors.reference: Journal of Crystal Growth 2013, substrate effect on CaCO3 crystallisation
literature_anchors.finding: surface chemistry, roughness and surface energy influence nucleation/adhesion; fluorinated DLC is cited as a route to lower scale adhesion

literature_anchors.reference: Advances in Colloid and Interface Science 324 (2024) 103090
literature_anchors.finding: superhydrophobic anti-fouling coatings are promising but practical durability remains a major engineering limitation

coupling_to_calcifer_self_maintenance.sequence: low-adhesion wall -> delayed/weak CaCO3 attachment -> Axle/wiper disrupts young scale -> centrifugal solids transport -> crystal trap -> washable filter
coupling_to_calcifer_self_maintenance.expected_system_effect: surface engineering reduces the amount of mechanical work required from Axle scraping and increases the fraction of calcium that can be redirected to serviceable crystal-trap locations
coupling_to_calcifer_self_maintenance.hard_boundary: The coating is a prevention layer, not a substitute for crystal traps, low-hardness make-up water, chemical compatibility control or mechanical cleaning.

measure: CaCO3 wall mass per area and time
shear or pull-off force required to detach deposit
POMS O2-flux change from any coating leachate or chemistry interaction

selection_metric: minimize persistent wall CaCO3 and detachment force while keeping coating wear, Axle torque, corrosion and O2-loop compatibility inside declared limits
next_gate: R0A4F1_SURFACE_COUPON_LONG_HOLD: compare bare, hard low-adhesion and superhydrophobic surfaces under representative water chemistry plus repeated Axle-wiper cycles, then feed measured adhesion and wear values into the long-hold Calcifer model.
